summary: Round 2, tests. All three arms of checkReader's new split are pinned in BOTH directions, measured by mutation in a copy of the staged tree. Round-1 major (empty arm judged only in the clean direction) is FIXED: re-adding `if (entries.isEmpty()) return found;` now kills anEMPTYOwnChainInheritsNOTHINGAndProductionAgrees. The author's five claimed mutations reproduce as killed, and the 'wrong epoch instead of none' probe the author asked for is killed too. One minor: the depth>1000 guard in Invariants.inheritedOffsets -- named load-bearing by the comment this commit ADDS at Invariants.java:274 -- is itself unconstrained; deleting it leaves the whole suite green.

findings.title: The depth guard this commit calls 'the guard that matters' is pinned by no test
findings.failure_scenario: The staged comment at Invariants.java:274-281 deletes offsetsSealedInto's own depth guard and justifies it: 'The guard that matters is on the recursion, which is `inheritedOffsets`', and `depth` is threaded through to reach it.' MEASURED in a copy of the staged tree: deleting `if (depth > 1000) { return inherited; }` from inheritedOffsets (Invariants.java:205-207) leaves `./gradlew :sequencer:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. So the surviving claim rests on prose only. The recursion it bounds is real: inheritedOffsets -> offsetsSealedInto(startFrom = opening.prevEpoch(), depth) -> inheritedOffsets(prior, from, depth+1), and unlike production's ChainReplay.replayAncestry (which THROWS on `opening.prevEpoch() >= chainEpoch`, its javadoc citing a measured two-object cycle that 'recursed until the stack went'), Invariants never checks that the link decreases -- checkLink reports the violation but the walk continues. A hand-built chain whose CONTINUE names its own epoch therefore recurses until StackOverflowError, and no test says so. Not major: no chain production can write reaches it, so the surviving mutant produces no wrong verdict on any input M4.13's sweep can generate today. A test feeding checkChain/checkReader a self-referencing Continue(0, epoch, seq) and asserting it terminates would close it.
findings.surviving_mutation: delete `if (depth > 1000) { return inherited; }` from Invariants.inheritedOffsets -- suite stays green

findings.title: Truncated first sentence left in the rewritten javadoc
findings.failure_scenario: The javadoc of theZOMBIEOnANeverOpenedChainIsReportedOnBOTHSides opens with the half-sentence 'THE WRITER'S SIDE OF THAT SAME HISTORY STAYS VISIBLE, which bounds how' and then restarts with a second warning marker on the next line. The old sentence's tail was replaced but its head was not deleted. No behaviour is affected and no mutation survives because of it; the cost is that the file whose stated job is recording WHY a case exists now carries a sentence that stops mid-clause, which is the artifact a later reader trusts.
findings.surviving_mutation: none -- documentation defect, no test weakened

notes: Three-case split, both directions per case: EMPTY -- clean pinned by ReaderView.of(reader) plus an independent assertion that production's own reader.offsets() is empty, broken pinned by ReaderView(9, {RA=3}) -> I3. SEALED-AT-0 -- correct/dropped/wild pinned to clean/I4/I3, with reader.offsets() containsEntry(RA,3) pinning the base value so an off-by-one in the walk shows as I3. CONTINUE arm -- broken pinned by aColdStartChainOpeningWithADELTAIsSTILLJudged, clean by ReaderInvariantsTest.aReaderThatSTOPSAtTheSealViolatesNothing and productionsOwnReader...

The empty arm cannot false-positive against a real reader: CommitLog.open (CommitLog.java:364) PUTs the CONTINUE before crossFrom sets offsets, so a reader never carries inherited offsets while its own chain is still empty. checkReader's origin/mid-ancestry asymmetry matches ChainReplay.neverOpened(first, atOrigin) exactly.

The removed `Verdict.judged()` assertions in ReaderInvariantsTest are not a weakened assertion: the type they read was deleted in the same commit and the claim could not go false. Not treated as the test-inversion check-test-integrity.sh is about.
